title: Pure water is only pH 7 at room temperature
body: Water molecules constantly split into H⁺ and OH⁻ ions and recombine. Pure water is neutral because those two ions are always present in equal amounts, but how many form depends on temperature. Around 25 °C neutral water has a pH of about 7, but at 100 °C more molecules break apart and neutral pH falls to about 6.1, while near 0 °C it is about 7.5. So boiling water isn’t acidic: the meaning of “neutral” simply shifts with temperature.

slides.question: What is the pH of pure, neutral water at 100 °C?
slides.explanation: About 6.1. At 100 °C more water molecules split into H⁺ and OH⁻, but the two are still present in equal amounts, so boiling water is neutral, not acidic.
